good_when: A maintainer weighing a change sees at a glance the one order in which all four key results rank, across both objectives: whether KR1.1 or KR2.1 wins when they pull against each other, and where KR1.2 and KR2.2 stand against each other, without piecing the order together from the two 'ranked after' notes and the sentence below the list.

The accounting team and invoicer's maintainers find the order in which the key results count in one place, and read from it alone which key result a change must not worsen before another may improve, including whether KR2.1 counts before or after KR1.2. Today KR1.2 and KR2.2 each say what they rank after, and the sentence below the list says again that KR1.1 and KR2.1 come first, so a reader pieces the order together from three places that could drift apart. Likewise, the help that O1 rules out reads the same wherever it is stated: O1 says without a developer's help, while KR1.1 counts invoices printed without any help.
